景裕雖不聚徒教授，所注易大行於世。 又好釋氏，通其大義。 天竺胡沙門道悕每論諸經論，輒託景裕為之序。 景裕之敗也。 繫晉陽獄，至心誦經，枷鎖自脫。 是時又有人負罪當死，夢沙門教講經，覺時如所夢，默誦千遍，臨刑刀折，主者以聞，赦之。 此經遂行於世，號曰高王觀世音。
Though Jingyu did not gather disciples to teach, his commentary on the Changes circulated widely. He also loved Buddhism and mastered its essential teachings. The Indian monk Daoxi always asked Jingyu to write prefaces whenever he lectured on the sutras and treatises. When Jingyu fell into adversity. He was imprisoned in the jail at Jinyang. Chanting sutras with utmost devotion, his cangue and fetters fell away by themselves. At that time another man condemned to death dreamed that a monk taught him to recite a sutra. Upon waking he did as in the dream and silently recited it a thousand times. At execution the blade broke; the official reported this and he was pardoned. This sutra then spread widely and came to be known as the Guanyin Sutra of the King of Gao.
56
李同軌，趙郡高邑人，陽夏太守義深之弟。 體貌魁岸，腰帶十圍，學綜諸經，多所治誦，兼讀釋氏，又好醫術。 年二十二，舉秀才，射策，除奉朝請，領國子助教。 轉著作郎，典儀注，修國史，遷國子博士，加征虜將軍。 永熙二年，出帝幸平等寺，僧徒講法，敕同軌論難，音韻閑朗，往復可觀，出帝善之。 三年春，釋菜，詔延公卿學官於顯陽殿，敕祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁講禮記，中書舍人盧景宣解大戴禮夏小正篇。 時廣招儒學，引令預聽。 同軌經義素優，辯析兼美，而不得執經，深為慨恨。 天平中，轉中書侍郎。 興和中，兼通直散騎常侍，使蕭衍。 衍深耽釋學，遂集名僧於其愛敬、同泰二寺，講𣵀盤大品經，引同軌預席。 衍兼遣其朝臣並共觀聽。 同軌論難久之，道俗咸以為善。 盧景裕卒，齊獻武王引同軌在館教諸公子，甚加禮之。 每旦入授，日暮始歸。 緇素請業者，同軌夜為說解，四時恒爾，不以為倦。 武定四年夏卒，年四十七。 時人傷惜之，齊獻武王亦殊嗟悼，贈襚甚厚。 贈驃騎大將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰康。
Li Tonggui was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery and the younger brother of Yishen, Administrator of Yangxia. He had an imposing physique and a waist ten wei around. He mastered the classics and had studied and recited many of them, also read Buddhist texts, and loved medicine. At twenty-two he was nominated as Outstanding Talent, passed the policy examination, was appointed Palace Attendant, and served concurrently as Assistant Erudite of the Imperial University. He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Library, directed ritual protocols, and compiled the national history. He was then promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University with the additional title General Who Subdues Barbarians. In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaojing visited Pingdeng Temple while monks were expounding the Dharma. He ordered Tonggui to engage in debate. Tonggui's voice was clear and measured, his exchanges impressive, and the emperor was pleased. In the spring of the third year, at the Confucian vegetable-offering ceremony, an edict summoned high ministers and academy officials to the Xianyang Hall. Chancellor Liu Yin was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yu on the Record of Rites, and Palace Secretary Attendant Lu Jingxuan to expound the Xiaxiaozheng chapter of Dai the Elder's Record of Rites. At the time the court was broadly recruiting Confucian scholars, and Tonggui was invited to attend and listen. Tonggui had long excelled in the meaning of the classics and was equally gifted in debate, yet he was never given the lectern himself—a source of deep regret. During the Tianping era he was transferred to the post of Palace Secretary Attendant. During the Xinghe era he additionally served as Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff and was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan. Xiao Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning. He gathered eminent monks at his Ai'jing and Tongtai monasteries to expound the Mahaparinirvana Great Vaipulya Sutra and invited Tonggui to join the assembly. Xiao Yan also sent his court officials to observe and listen together. Tonggui debated at length, and both clergy and laypeople alike praised his performance. After Lu Jingyu died, King Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into his household to instruct the princes and treated him with exceptional respect. Each morning he entered to teach and did not return until dusk. For those who sought instruction, whether monks or laypeople, Tonggui would lecture and explain at night. He did this through all four seasons without ever tiring of it. He died in the summer of the fourth year of Wuding, at the age of forty-seven. People of the time mourned his loss. King Xianwu of Qi also grieved for him deeply, and the funeral gifts were exceptionally generous. He was posthumously granted the titles General-in-Chief of Rapid Cavalry and Inspector of Ying Prefecture, with the posthumous name Kang.
57
李業興，上黨長子人也。 祖虬，父玄紀，並以儒學舉孝廉。 玄紀卒於金鄉令。 業興少耿介，志學精力，負帙從師，不憚勤苦。 耽思章句，好覽異說。 晚乃師事徐遵明於趙魏之間。 時有漁陽鮮于靈馥亦聚徒教授，而遵明聲譽未高，著錄尚寡。 業興乃詣靈馥黌舍，類受業者。 靈馥乃謂曰：「李生久逐羌博士，何所得也？ 」業興默爾不言。 及靈馥說左傳，業興問其大義數條，靈馥不能對。 於是振衣而起曰：「羌弟子正如此耳！ 」遂便徑還。 自此靈馥生徒傾學而就遵明。 遵明學徒大盛，業興之為也。
Li Yexing was a native of Changzi in Shangdang Commandery. His grandfather Qiu and his father Xuanji had both been nominated as Filial and Incorrupt on the strength of their Confucian learning. Xuanji died while serving as magistrate of Jinxiang. From youth Yexing was upright and resolute. He pursued learning with great energy, carrying his books to follow his teachers and never shrinking from toil or hardship. He immersed himself in textual commentary and loved to read divergent interpretations. Only later did he take Xu Zunming as his teacher in the region between Zhao and Wei. At the time Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also gathered disciples to teach, while Xu Zunming's reputation was not yet established and his enrollment remained small. Yexing then went to Lingfu's school, appearing for all the world like an ordinary student. Lingfu then said to him, "Scholar Li, you have long followed the Qiang Doctor—what have you learned from him? " Yexing said nothing and remained silent. When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo Commentary, Yexing asked several questions about its broader meaning, which Lingfu could not answer. Thereupon Yexing shook out his robes and rose, saying, "A disciple of the Qiang is just like this! " Then he went straight home. From that point on, Lingfu's students abandoned him and flocked to Xu Zunming. Xu Zunming's following grew immensely—and it was Yexing who made it happen.
58
後乃博涉百家，圖緯、風角、天文、占候無不詳練，尤長算歷。 雖在貧賤，常自矜負，若禮待不足，縱於權貴，不為之屈。 後為王遵業門客。 舉孝廉，為校書郎。 以世行趙𢾺曆，節氣後辰下算，延昌中，業興乃為戊子元曆上之。 於時屯騎校尉張洪、盪寇將軍張龍祥等九家各獻新曆，世宗詔令共為一曆。 洪等後遂共推業興為主，成戊子曆，[9]正光三年奏行之。 事在律曆志。 累遷奉朝請。 臨淮王彧征蠻，引為騎兵參軍。 後廣陵王淵北征，復為外兵參軍。 業興以殷曆甲寅，黃帝辛卯，徒有積元，術數亡缺，業興又修之，各為一卷，傳於世。
Later he mastered a wide range of learning. Cosmological apocrypha, wind-direction divination, astronomy, and prognostication—none lay beyond his detailed command—and he was especially expert in calendrical calculation. Though poor and of humble station, he held himself in high regard. If he felt he had not been shown sufficient courtesy, he would not yield even to the powerful and noble. Later he became a retainer in the household of Wang Zunye. Nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed Proofreader. Because the Zhao calendar then in use lagged behind the solar terms in its calculations, during the Yanchang era Yexing composed the Wuzi Origin Calendar and submitted it to the throne. At that time Commandant of Attendant Cavalry Zhang Hong, General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Longxiang, and eight other families each submitted new calendars. Emperor Shizong ordered that they be combined into a single calendar. Hong and the others later jointly recommended Yexing to lead the effort, completing the Wuzi Calendar. [9] It was submitted and put into use in the third year of Zhenguang. The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Calendars and Astronomy. He was promoted in succession to the post of Palace Attendant. When Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu campaigned against the southern barbarians, he recruited Yexing as Cavalry Army Adjutant. Later, when Prince of Guangling Yuan Yuan campaigned north, he again served as Adjutant of External Troops. Yexing held that the Yin Calendar of the Jiayin era and the Yellow Emperor Xinyin calendar possessed accumulated origin-years in name only, while their calendrical methods were lost and defective. He revised them, each in one scroll, and they were handed down in the world.
59
建義初，敕典儀注，未幾除著作佐郎。 永安二年，以前造曆之勳，賜爵長子伯。 遭憂解任，尋起復本官。 元曄之竊號也，除通直散騎侍郎。 普泰元年，沙汰侍官，業興仍在通直，加寧朔將軍。 又除征虜將軍、中散大夫，仍在通直。 太昌初，轉散騎侍郎，仍以典儀之勤，特賞一階，除平東將軍、光祿大夫，尋加安西將軍。 後以出帝登極之初，預行禮事，封屯留縣開國子，食邑五百戶。 轉中軍將軍、通直散騎常侍。 永熙三年二月，出帝釋奠，業興與魏季景、溫子昇、竇瑗為摘句。 後入為侍讀。
At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was ordered to direct ritual protocols. Before long he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library. In the second year of Yong'an, for his earlier merit in creating the calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Changzi. He resigned to observe mourning, then soon returned to his original post. When Yuan Ye usurped the imperial title, Yexing was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Privy Staff. In the first year of Putai, when attendant officials were culled, Yexing retained his post in the Privy Staff and received the additional title General Who Pacifies the North. He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Palace Attendant Grandee, while continuing to serve in the Privy Staff. At the beginning of the Taichang era he was transferred to Attendant Cavalry Gentleman. For his diligence in directing rituals he was specially rewarded one rank and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Household Grandee; soon after he received the additional title General Who Pacifies the West. Later, because he had taken part in ritual affairs at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's accession, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tunliu with an estate of five hundred households. He was transferred to General of the Central Army and Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff. In the second month of the third year of Yongxi, at Emperor Xiaowu's Confucian temple sacrifice, Yexing served as excerpt presenter together with Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan. Later he entered court service as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
60
遷鄴之始，起部郎中辛術奏曰：「今皇居徙御，百度創始，營構一興，必宜中制。 上則憲章前代，下則模寫洛京。 今鄴都雖舊，基址毀滅，又圖記參差，事宜審定。 臣雖曰職司，學不稽古，國家大事非敢專之。 通直散騎常侍李業興碩學通儒，博聞多識，萬門千戶，所宜訪詢。 今求就之披圖案記，考定是非，參古雜今，折中為制，召畫工并所須調度，具造新圖，申奏取定。 庶經始之日，執事無疑。 」詔從之。 天平二年，除鎮南將軍，尋為侍讀。 於時尚書右僕射、營構大將高隆之被詔繕治三署樂器、衣服及百戲之屬，乃奏請業興共參其事。
At the beginning of the move to Ye, Director of the Bureau of Construction Xin Shu memorialized, saying, "Now that the imperial residence is being relocated and every institution is being newly established, once construction begins it must conform to a central standard. Above, it should take the former dynasties as its model; below, it should replicate the layout of Luoyang. Although Ye is an old capital, its foundations have been destroyed, and the maps and records are inconsistent. The matter requires careful determination. Though I hold this office, my learning does not reach back to antiquity, and I dare not decide a matter of such national importance on my own. Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff Li Yexing is a great scholar and thorough Confucian, broad in learning and rich in knowledge. Matters of palace layout and urban design are precisely what he should be consulted about. I now request that he be summoned to examine the maps and records, determine what is correct and incorrect, compare antiquity with the present and strike a balanced standard, summon painters together with whatever supplies are needed, produce complete new plans, and submit them for imperial approval. Thus when construction begins, those in charge will have no doubts. " An edict approved the proposal. In the second year of Tianping he was appointed General Who Guards the South; soon after he became Lecturer-in-Waiting. At that time Executive Assistant of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, commissioned as Grand General of Construction, received an edict to repair the instruments, garments, and variety-show accoutrements of the Three Bureaus. He then memorialized asking that Yexing participate jointly in the work.
61
四年，與兼散騎常侍李諧、[10]兼吏部郎盧元明使蕭衍。 衍散騎常侍朱异問業興曰：「魏洛中委粟山是南郊邪？ 」業興曰：「委粟是圓丘，非南郊。 」异曰：「北間郊、丘異所，是用鄭義。 我此中用王義。 」業興曰：「然，洛京郊、丘之處專用鄭解。 」异曰：「若然，女子逆降傍親亦從鄭以不？ 」業興曰：「此之一事，亦不專從。 若卿此間用王義，除禫應用二十五月，何以王儉喪禮禫用二十七月也？ 」异遂不答。 業興曰：「我昨見明堂四柱方屋，都無五九之室，當是裴頠所制。 明堂上圓下方，裴唯除室耳。 今此上不圓何也？ 」异曰：「圓方之說，經典無文，何怪於方？ 」業興曰：「圓方之言，出處甚明，卿自不見。 見卿錄梁主孝經義亦云上圓下方，卿言豈非自相矛盾！ 」异曰：「若然，圓方竟出何經？ 」業興曰：「出孝經援神契。 」异曰：「緯候之書，何用信也！ 」業興曰：「卿若不信，靈威仰、叶光紀之類經典亦無出者，卿復信不？ 」异不答。
In the fourth year he went as envoy to Xiao Yan together with Concurrent Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Li He, [10] and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Yuanming. Xiao Yan's Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Zhu Yi asked Yexing, "In Wei Luoyang, is Mount Weisu the Southern Suburb? " Yexing said, "Weisu is the Round Mound, not the Southern Suburb. " Yi said, "In the North the suburban altar and the mound are at separate sites—that follows Zheng Xuan's interpretation. Here we follow Wang Su's interpretation. " Yexing said, "Indeed—in Luoyang the sites of the suburban altar and the mound exclusively follow Zheng's explanation. " Yi said, "If so, in the matter of a woman's descending in mourning rank for collateral relatives, do you also follow Zheng? " Yexing said, "In this one matter, we do not exclusively follow him either. If here you follow Wang's interpretation, the end of mourning should come in the twenty-fifth month—so why did Wang Jian's Mourning Rites prescribe the twenty-seventh month for ending mourning? " Yi made no reply. Yexing said, "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—a square hall on four pillars—with none of the five-by-nine chambers. It must be the design of Pei Yin. The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers. Why is this one not round above? " Yi said, "The round-and-square doctrine has no textual basis in the classics—what is strange about square? " Yexing said, "The round-and-square doctrine is very clearly attested in its sources—you simply have not seen them. I see that in your record of the Liang ruler's Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety it also says round above and square below—are your words not self-contradictory! " Yi said, "If so, from which classic does the round-and-square doctrine ultimately come? " Yexing said, "It comes from the Apocryphal Text on the Classic of Filial Piety Supporting the Divine Covenant. " Yi said, "Why should one trust books of cosmological apocrypha and prognostication! " Yexing said, "If you do not believe, texts like the Lingweiyang and the Yeguangji likewise have no attestation in the classics—do you believe in them or not? " Yi made no reply.
62
蕭衍親問業興曰：「聞卿善於經義，儒、玄之中何所通達？ 」業興曰：「少為書生，止讀五典，至於深義，不辨通釋。 」衍問：「詩周南，王者之風，繫之周公； 邵南，仁賢之風，繫之邵公。 何名為繫？ 」業興對曰：「鄭注儀禮云：昔大王、王季居于岐陽，躬行邵南之教，以興王業。 及文王行今周南之教以受命。 作邑於酆，分其故地，屬之二公。 名為繫。 」衍又問：「若是故地，應自統攝，何由分封二公？ 」業興曰：「文王為諸侯之時所化之本國，今既登九五之尊，不可復守諸侯之地，故分封二公。 」衍又問：「乾卦初稱『潛龍』，二稱『見龍』，至五『飛龍』。 初可名為虎。 」問意小乖。 業興對：「學識膚淺，不足仰酬。 」衍又問：「尚書『正月上日受終文祖』，此是何正？ 」業興對：「此是夏正月。 」衍言何以得知。 業興曰：「案尚書中候運行篇云『日月營始』，故知夏正。 」衍又問：「堯時以何月為正？ 」業興對：「自堯以上，書典不載，實所不知。 」衍又云：「『寅賓出日』，即是正月。 『日中星鳥，以殷仲春』，即是二月。 此出堯典，何得云堯時不知用何正也？ 」業興對：「雖三正不同，言時節者皆據夏時正月。 周禮，仲春二月會男女之無夫家者。 雖自周書，月亦夏時。 堯之日月，亦當如此。 但所見不深，無以辨析明問。 」衍又曰：「禮，原壤之母死，孔子助其沐椁。 原壤叩木而歌曰：『久矣夫，予之不託於音也。 [11]狸首之班然，執女手之卷然。 』孔子聖人，而與原壤為友？ 」業興對：「孔子即自解，言親者不失其為親，故者不失其為故。 」又問：「原壤何處人？ 」業興對曰：「鄭注云：原壤，孔子幼少之舊。 故是魯人。 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，所存必可法。 原壤不孝，有逆人倫，何以存故舊之小節，廢不孝之大罪？ 」業興對曰：「原壤所行，事自彰著。 幼少之交，非是今始，既無大故，何容棄之？ 孔子深敦故舊之義，於理無失。 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，何以書原壤之事，垂法萬代？ 」業興對曰：「此是後人所錄，非孔子自制。 猶合葬於防，如此之類，禮記之中動有百數。 」衍又問：「易曰太極，是有無？ 」業興對：「所傳太極是有，素不玄學，何敢輒酬。」
Xiao Yan personally asked Yexing, "I hear you are skilled in the meaning of the classics—in Confucian and Dark Learning alike, what do you comprehend? " Yexing said, "In youth I was a scholar who read only the Five Classics. As for their deeper meaning, I cannot distinguish or explain it thoroughly. " Yan asked, "In the Poetry, Zhou Nan is the air of the kingly way and is attributed to the Duke of Zhou; Shao Nan is the air of humane worthies and is attributed to the Duke of Shao. What is meant by 'attributed'? " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites says: In former times King Da and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally carried out the teachings of Shao Nan to raise up the royal enterprise. When King Wen carried out the teachings of Zhou Nan as they are today, he received the Mandate. He established his capital at Feng and divided the former territory, assigning portions to the two dukes. This is what is meant by 'attributed.' " Yan asked again, "If it was former territory, he should have governed it himself—how could he enfeoff the two dukes? " Yexing said, "It was the homeland over which Wen had exercised transforming influence while still a feudal lord. Now that he had ascended to supreme dignity, he could no longer hold feudal territory himself, and so he enfeoffed the two dukes. " Yan asked again, "In the Qian hexagram the first line is called 'Hidden Dragon,' the second 'Dragon Appears,' and by the fifth 'Flying Dragon.' The first could be called a tiger. The intent of the question was slightly off. Yexing replied, "My learning is shallow and superficial—not adequate to meet your question worthily. " Yan asked again, "In the Documents, 'On the first day of the first month he received the end from Wen the Ancestor'—which first month is this? " Yexing replied, "This is the first month of the Xia calendar. " Yan asked how he knew this. Yexing said, "According to the Running Phases chapter of the Apocryphal Documents on the Middle Calendars, which says 'The sun and moon set out at the beginning,' one knows it is the Xia first month. " Yan asked again, "In Yao's time, which month served as the first month? " Yexing replied, "From Yao and earlier, the canonical texts do not record this—I truly do not know. " Yan also said, "'The day is respectfully received at the coming-out of the sun at yin'—that is the first month. 'When the sun is at mid-heaven and the Star Bird is seen, it is truly mid-spring'—that is the second month. This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say that in Yao's time one did not know which month served as the first? " Yexing replied, "Although the Three First Months differ, when speaking of seasons one always takes the Xia calendar's first month as the basis. In the Rites of Zhou, in the second month of mid-spring men and women without spouses are brought together. Although this comes from the Zhou Documents, the month referred to is still the Xia calendar. Yao's sun and moon should likewise be so. But my reading is not deep enough to analyze and answer your clear question. " Yan also said, "In the Ritual Records, when Yuan Rang's mother died, Confucius helped him prepare the bathing and coffining. Yuan Rang knocked on the coffin board and sang, 'Long has it been since I have not entrusted myself to music. [11] Like the spotted pattern of an otter's head, curled as a woman's hand. ' Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Yuan Rang? " Yexing replied, "Confucius himself explained that kin do not cease to be kin, nor do old acquaintances cease to be old acquaintances. " He asked again, "Where was Yuan Rang from? " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary says: Yuan Rang was an old friend from Confucius's youth. Therefore he was a man of Lu. " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—surely what he preserved is worthy of emulation. Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why preserve a small point of old friendship and set aside the great crime of unfiliality? " Yexing replied, "Yuan Rang's conduct speaks for itself and is manifest. The friendship of youth did not begin only now—there was no grave cause; how could it be abandoned? Confucius deeply honored the meaning of old friendship—there is no fault in principle. " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—why record the affair of Yuan Rang and hand down a model for ten thousand generations? " Yexing replied, "This was recorded by later men—it was not composed by Confucius himself. Such matters as joint burial at Fang—of this sort there are easily a hundred in the Book of Rites. " Yan asked again, "The Changes says Supreme Polarity—is it being or non-being? " Yexing replied, "According to tradition Supreme Polarity is being—I have never studied Dark Learning, so how dare I answer offhand."
63
業興愛好墳籍，鳩集不已，手自補治，躬加題帖，其家所有，垂將萬卷。 覽讀不息，多有異聞，諸儒服其淵博。 性豪俠，重意氣。 人有急難，委之歸命，便能容匿。 與其好合，傾身無吝。 若有相乖忤，便即疵毀，乃至聲色，加以謗罵。 性又躁隘，至於論難之際，高聲攘振，無儒者之風。 每語人云：「但道我好，雖知妄言，故勝道惡。 」務進忌前，不顧後患，時人以此惡之。 至於學術精微，當時莫及。
Yexing loved ancient texts and collected them without cease, personally mending and restoring them and adding title slips with his own hand. His household holdings approached ten thousand scrolls. He read incessantly, hearing much that was unusual, and the Confucian scholars admired his profound erudition. By nature he was bold and chivalrous, placing great weight on loyalty and friendship. When men faced urgent distress and entrusted themselves to him for refuge, he could shelter them. With those he favored he was wholeheartedly generous without stint. If there was friction, he would immediately find fault and pick at them, even raising his voice and adding slander and abuse. His nature was also rash and narrow—during debates he would raise his voice and gesticulate wildly, without the bearing of a Confucian scholar. He often told people, "Just say I'm good—even though you know it is false talk, it still beats saying I'm bad. " He strove to advance, resented those ahead of him, and gave no thought to later troubles; people at the time hated him for this. As for the subtle depths of learning, no one of the time could match him.
64
子崇祖，武定中，太尉外兵參軍。
His son Chongzu served as External Troops Aide to the Grand Marshal during the Wuding era.
65
崇祖弟遵祖，太昌中，業興傳其長子伯以授之。 齊受禪，例降。
Chongzu's younger brother Zunzu—in the Taichang era Yexing had his eldest son Bo pass down the family learning and entrusted it to him. When Qi received the abdication, he was reduced in rank by precedent.
66
史臣曰：古語云：容體不足觀，勇力不足恃，族姓不足道，先祖不足稱，然而顯聞四方，流聲後裔者，其惟學乎。 信哉斯言也。 梁越之徒，篤志不倦，自求諸己，遂能聞道下風，稱珍席上，或聚徒千百，或服冕乘軒，咸稽古之力也。
The historiographer remarks: An ancient saying runs, "Physique is not worth looking at, courage and strength are not worth relying on, clan and surname are not worth mentioning, and forebears are not worth boasting of—yet to be renowned in all directions and leave a name to posterity, is it not through learning?" How true these words are! Men such as Liang Yue devoted themselves tirelessly, seeking within themselves, and were thus able to hear the Way and attend lectures from below, to be prized at the lectern. Some gathered hundreds or thousands of disciples, others wore regalia and rode in chariots—all owed to the power of studying antiquity.
67
校勘記
Collation Notes
68
魏書卷八十四諸本目錄此卷注「不全」，卷末有宋人校語云：「高氏小史儒林傳無刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌三人，史目錄皆有之。 此卷刁沖、盧景裕傳全錄北史，非魏收書，史臣論亦出北史，北史全用隋書傳論。 」殿本以校語入考證，開頭一句又改成「魏收書儒林傳亡，用高氏小史補之」。 按此卷常爽、刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌四傳，北史卷八一儒林傳所無。 常爽，北史卷四二有專傳，刁沖附卷二六刁雍傳，盧景裕附卷三０盧同傳，李同軌附卷三三李義深傳。 今檢此卷常爽傳也全同北史，宋人漏舉。 李同軌則魏書本已附卷三六李順傳，與此卷同軌傳幾乎全同，一人二傳，實為重出 〈北史同軌傳較簡〉 。 其他諸傳，凡北史儒林傳所有諸人都比北史詳備。 其中徐遵明傳，北史多出勒索學生事，李業興傳多出語音不正和與孫騰、邢子才對答語，當是北史據其他材料增入，非魏書原文所有。 傳序也像是北史傳序敍魏事一段所本。 據上述情況，除常、刁、盧三傳及史論外，似皆魏書原文。 宋人於目錄注「不全」，於校語只說刁、盧二傳「非魏收書」，史臣論「出北史」，則也認為序和其他諸傳是魏書原文。 且據校語，當時比對高氏小史，只說三傳此有彼無，沒有說其他諸傳以小史補。 小史久亡，清人又何從知之？ 但也有可疑之處：一，若說此卷只是殘缺不全，除三傳外均魏書原文，何以所缺前後錯出，恰好是北史儒林傳所無之傳？ 高氏小史節錄魏書，何以小史儒林傳所無的三傳也是北史儒林傳所無？ 二，李同軌，魏書已附李順傳，儒林傳目應無其名，何以校語說「史目錄有之」？ 或此所謂「史目錄」乃指宗諫史目等 〈見卷八六孝感傳按語〉 ，則後人據目補傳，何以不據本書目錄而據他書？ 後人既已從李順傳中析出同軌傳入儒林，何以不刪李順傳中所有？ 這些疑問頗難解釋。
Book of Wei, juan 84: the table of contents in various editions notes this juan as "incomplete." At the end of the juan is a Song-dynasty collation note that reads, "The Confucian Scholars section of Gao's Brief History lacks the three men Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui, but the History's table of contents lists them all. The biographies of Diao Chong and Lu Jingyu in this juan are copied entirely from the History of the Northern Dynasties and are not from Wei Shou's book. The historiographer's comment also comes from the Northern History, which in turn wholly adopts the biographical commentaries of the History of the Sui. " The Palace Edition incorporated the collation note into its textual verification and changed the opening sentence to "Wei Shou's Confucian Scholars section is lost; it was supplemented from Gao's Brief History." According to this, the four biographies of Chang Shuang, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui in this juan are absent from the Confucian Scholars section in juan 81 of the Northern History. Chang Shuang has a separate biography in juan 42 of the Northern History. Diao Chong is appended to the biography of Diao Yong in juan 26; Lu Jingyu is appended to the biography of Lu Tong in juan 30; Li Tonggui is appended to the biography of Li Yishen in juan 33. On examination, the biography of Chang Shuang in this juan is also identical to the Northern History—the Song editors omitted mention of it. Li Tonggui, meanwhile, was already appended to the biography of Li Shun in juan 36 of the original Book of Wei. The Tonggui biography in this juan is nearly identical—one man with two biographies, a true duplication 〈The Northern History Tonggui biography is briefer〉 . The other biographies—all the men who appear in the Northern History's Confucian Scholars section—are more detailed here than in the Northern History. Among them, the biography of Xu Zunming in the Northern History adds the affair of extorting students. The biography of Li Yexing adds incorrect pronunciation and exchanges with Sun Teng and Xing Zicai—these were likely added by the Northern History from other materials and are not in the original Book of Wei text. The preface to the biographies also appears to be the source for the Northern History's preface section narrating Wei affairs. According to the above, apart from the three biographies of Chang, Diao, and Lu and the historiographer's comment, all seem to be original Book of Wei text. The Song editors noted "incomplete" in the table of contents. In the collation note they said only that the Diao and Lu biographies were "not Wei Shou's book" and that the historiographer's comment "came from the Northern History"—thus they too considered the preface and the other biographies to be original Book of Wei text. Moreover, according to the collation note, when Gao's Brief History was compared at the time, it was said only that the three biographies were present here but absent there—nothing was said about other biographies being supplemented from the Brief History. The Brief History has long been lost—how could Qing scholars have known this? Yet there are also points of doubt: First, if this juan is merely incomplete and all except the three biographies are original Book of Wei text, why are the missing portions scattered before and after, and why do they happen to be precisely the biographies absent from the Northern History's Confucian Scholars section? Gao's Brief History abridges the Book of Wei—so why are the three biographies absent from the Brief History's Confucian Scholars section also absent from the Northern History's Confucian Scholars section? Second, Li Tonggui was already appended to Li Shun's biography in the Book of Wei—the Confucian Scholars table of contents should not list his name—so why does the collation note say "the History's table of contents lists him"? Perhaps the so-called "History's table of contents" refers to such works as Zong Jian's Catalog of Histories 〈See the editorial note to the Filial Conduct section, juan 86〉 , then when later men supplemented biographies according to a catalog, why did they rely on another book's catalog rather than this book's own? Since later men had already extracted the Tonggui biography from Li Shun's biography and placed it in the Confucian Scholars section, why did they not delete it from Li Shun's biography? These questions are quite difficult to explain.
69
河間邢祐諸本「祐」作「祜」，北史卷八一平恒傳作「祐」。 按邢祐附本書卷六五、北史卷四三邢巒傳，都作「祐」。 「祜」字訛，今據改。 下同。
Regarding Xing You of Hejian: various editions write "You" as "Hu"; the biography of Ping Heng in juan 81 of the Northern History reads "You." According to the appended biography of Xing You in juan 65 of this book and the biography of Xing Luan in juan 43 of the Northern History, both read "You." The character "Hu" is erroneous; the text is corrected here accordingly. The same applies below.
70
燕東部侯釐通鑑卷九八 〈三一０四頁〉 見燕「中部俟釐慕輿句」。 晉書卷一一０慕容儁載記無文，通鑑當據十六國春秋或范享燕書。 按突厥官有「俟利發」，契丹有「夷離堇」，並即此「俟釐」，這裏「侯」字當是「俟」的形訛。
Regarding the Eastern Department Marquis Li of Yan: Zizhi Tongjian, juan 98 〈page 3104〉 See the Yan passage on "Central Department Sili Muyu Ju." Jin Shu, juan 110, Annals of Murong Jun, has no such text. The Zizhi Tongjian likely draws on the Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms or Fan Xiang's Book of Yan. According to this, among Turkic offices there is "Siliba," and among the Khitan there is "Yilijin"—both correspond to this "Sili." Here the character "Hou" must be a graphic error for "Si."
71
見臯魚之歎方歸而養親諸本「臯」作「旱」。 北史卷八一劉獻之傳南本、殿本「旱」作「臯」。 按臯魚事見韓詩外傳卷九，云「於是門人辭歸而養親者十有三人」，與此傳語合。 「旱」字訛，今據改。
Regarding "seeing Gao Yu's sigh and then returning home to support his parents": various editions write "Gao" as "Han." In the biography of Liu Xianzhi in juan 81 of the Northern History, the Southern Edition and Palace Edition read "Han" as "Gao." According to this, the affair of Gao Yu appears in juan 9 of the Outer Commentary to the Han Poetry, which says, "Thereupon thirteen disciples took leave and returned home to support their parents"—this matches the language of this biography. The character "Han" is erroneous; the text is corrected here accordingly.
72
贈大將軍北史卷八一孫惠蔚傳無「大將軍」三字。 按大將軍甚重，以崔亮、崔光之顯貴，死後追贈亦只車騎、驃騎大將軍，孫惠蔚軍號為平東將軍，豈能驟贈此官。 疑是衍文，或「大」乃「本」之訛。
Regarding "posthumously enfeoffed as Grand General": the biography of Sun Huiwei in juan 81 of the Northern History lacks the three characters "Grand General." According to this, Grand General is a very exalted rank—even men as eminent as Cui Liang and Cui Guang received posthumously only General of Chariots and Cavalry or General of Agile Cavalry after death. Sun Huiwei's military title was General Who Pacifies the East—how could he suddenly be granted this office? This is suspected to be an interpolation, or "Grand" may be an error for "original."
73
刺史河東裴植並徵沖為功曹諸本和北史卷二六刁雍附刁沖傳「植」作「桓」。 張森楷云：「『桓』當作『植』，植傳 〈附卷七一裴叔業傳〉 除瀛州刺史，即此時事。 」按前劉蘭傳亦見瀛州刺史裴植。 刁沖稱勃海饒安人。 卷一０六上地形志上滄州條和浮陽郡饒安條，熙平二年 〈五一七〉 分置滄州前，饒安屬瀛州浮陽郡，其稱「勃海」，乃因漢晉舊屬。 裴植為瀛州刺史在熙平前，饒安是瀛州縣，刁沖是本州人，故得為功曹。 張說是，今改正。
Regarding "Grand Administrator Pei Zhi of Hedong also summoned Chong as Records Aide": various editions and the appended biography of Diao Chong to Diao Yong in juan 26 of the Northern History read "Zhi" as "Huan." Zhang Senkai said, "'Huan' should read 'Zhi'; Pei Zhi's biography 〈appended to juan 71, biography of Pei Shuye〉 records his appointment as Grand Administrator of Yingzhou—this is the affair in question. " According to this, the earlier biography of Liu Lan also mentions Pei Zhi as Grand Administrator of Yingzhou. Diao Chong is described as a native of Rao'an in Bohai. The entries for Cangzhou and for Rao'an in Fuyang Commandery in juan 106A of the Treatise on Geography, second year of Xiping 〈517〉 before Cangzhou was separately established, Rao'an belonged to Fuyang Commandery in Yingzhou. The designation "Bohai" derives from its former Han and Jin affiliation. Pei Zhi served as Grand Administrator of Yingzhou before Xiping. Rao'an was a county of Yingzhou, and Diao Chong was a native of that province—thus he could serve as Records Aide. Zhang's explanation is correct; the text is corrected here.
74
國子博士高涼及范陽盧道侃張森楷云：「『涼』當作『諒』。 據高佑傳 〈卷五七〉 ，佑孫諒為國子博士，在孝文、宣武間，與刁沖同時，當即其人。」
Regarding "Erudite of the National University Gao Liang and Lu Daokan of Fanyang": Zhang Senkai said, "'Liang' should read 'Liang' (the latter being the personal name Liang). According to the biography of Gao You 〈juan 57〉 You's grandson Liang served as erudite of the National University between Emperors Xiaowen and Xuanwu, contemporary with Diao Chong—he must be the man intended."
75
初元顥入洛諸本無「初」字，北史卷三０盧同附盧景裕傳有。 元顥事在前，前文敍事已至東魏末高澄當國時，李慈銘、張森楷均謂有誤。 李且謂「除國子博士前已載之，何必複出，北史於『元顥』上加一『初』字亦非。 」按這是追敍以前官位升退，刁沖「未曾有得失之色」，本非記歷官。 此傳本出北史，乃是脫「初」字，遂似敍事顛倒，今據補。
Regarding "when Yuan Hao first entered Luoyang": various editions lack the word "first"; the appended biography of Lu Jingyu in juan 30 of the Northern History includes it. Yuan Hao's affair belongs earlier, yet the preceding narrative already reaches Gao Cheng's dominance at the end of Eastern Wei; Li Ciming and Zhang Senkai both regard this as an error. Li further argued that the account of his dismissal as National University erudite was already given and need not be repeated, and that adding "first" before "Yuan Hao" in the Northern History is likewise wrong. This passage retrospectively recounts earlier promotions and demotions; Diao Chong "never showed the look of gain or loss"—it was never intended as a chronicle of official posts. This biography derives from the Northern History; the word "first" was dropped, making the narrative seem reversed—the text is restored here accordingly.
76
成戊子曆按卷一０七律曆志載崔光表云：「總合九家，共成一曆，元起壬子，律始黃鍾。 」業興初造之曆起於戊子，為戊子曆，至是「總合九家」則起於壬子，為壬子曆。 卷八二常景傳亦稱「先是參議正光壬子曆」可證。 這裏「戊子」乃「壬子」之訛。
Regarding "completing the Wuzi Calendar": the Treatise on Calendars in juan 10 records Cui Guang's memorial: "Combining nine schools into one calendar, the era begins at renzi and the pitch standard at Yellow Bell." Yexing's original calendar began at wuzi and was called the Wuzi Calendar; when the nine schools were combined, it began at renzi and became the Renzi Calendar. The biography of Chang Jing in juan 82 also refers to "earlier participation in deliberating the Zhengguang Renzi Calendar," which confirms this. Here "wuzi" is a scribal error for "renzi."
77
與兼散騎常侍李諧諸本脫「散」字，今據北史卷八一李業興傳補。
Regarding "together with Concurrent Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry Li Xie": various editions omit "Scattered"; restored according to the biography of Li Yexing in juan 81 of the Northern History.
78
久矣夫予之不託於音也諸本此句作「久矣，不託音」。 冊府卷六五八 〈七八七七頁〉 如上摘句。 按語出禮記檀弓下，諸本有脫文，今據補。
Regarding "Long has it been that I have not entrusted myself to music": various editions read this line as "Long indeed—not entrusted to music." Cefu, juan 658 〈page 7877〉 As quoted above. The words come from the Tan Gong chapter of the Record of Rites; various editions have lacunae, restored here accordingly.
